chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Umarah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
'The Divine proof of God cannot be established upon His creation except through an Imam, so that He may be recognized.'

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: Imam — in this context, the divinely appointed successor of the Prophet from Ahl al-Bayt; the locus of religious authority and the manifestation of God's proof
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: Hujja — the Divine proof or authority; in Shia theology, the term refers to one who establishes God's case upon His creation and serves as the channel of divine guidance
key_terms.يُعْرَفَ: to be recognized/known — refers to the gnosis (ma'rifa) of God being transmitted through the Imam, without whom humanity cannot truly know God

ai.seo_question: Why is an Imam necessary in Shia Islam for establishing divine proof?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam Ali al-Rida (the eighth Imam) articulates a foundational Shia theological doctrine: that divine guidance and the establishment of God's proof upon humanity is contingent upon the presence of an Imam. The Imam functions as the indispensable mediating authority through whom God's will is made known to creation. This teaching was directed to early Shia communities who were grappling with questions of religious authority and the necessity of continued Imamate after the Prophet.
